Sleeping Beauty. A three-act classical ballet composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, with scenario and choreography originally designed by Marius Petipa. Based on Charles Perrault's classic fairy tale, it premiered in 1890 at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg and showcased the peak of Imperial Russian ballet technique. The wicked fairy Carabosse curses the infant Princess Aurora to die on her sixteenth birthday by pricking her finger on a spindle. However, the benevolent Lilac Fairy softens the curse so that Aurora will not die but instead fall into a hundred-year sleep. The first act features the famous Rose Adagio, a technically demanding dance where Princess Aurora balances on one leg while receiving roses from four different suitors. The third act showcases a grand wedding celebration that features guest appearances from other fairy tale characters, including Puss in Boots and Little Red Riding Hood, expanding the world of the ballet beyond Aurora's story alone. Sleeping Beauty stands as the second of Tchaikovsky's three major ballet scores. The composer's symphonic approach to ballet composition would deeply influence classical ballet for generations to come, particularly in how music and dance narrative could be woven together into a unified artistic statement.
